documents.title: Discharge Summary - Lower GI Bleeding
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 01/07/2025  Discharge 01/09/2025

Reason for admission: recurrent painless bright red blood per rectum, onset the night before admission, in a 74-year-old man with a mechanical mitral valve on warfarin and aspirin. Colonoscopy 12/10/2024 during a quiet period found no source.

Allergies: NKDA.

Course:
- Hemodynamically stable on arrival. Hemoglobin followed every 8 hours, stayed close to his recent baseline; no transfusion required.
- Warfarin held on admission; heparin infusion started once INR fell below goal, paused for procedures.
- Nuclear medicine tagged red blood cell scan 01/07: radiotracer activity localizing to the cecum, suggesting a cecal bleeding source.
- Colonoscopy 01/08, while still passing blood: several small, flat, bright cherry-red spots in the cecum made up of dilated ectatic vessels - angiodysplasia; treated with argon plasma coagulation with good effect. No other source.
- Bleeding stopped after treatment. Warfarin resumed 01/08 evening with heparin overlap; discharged on enoxaparin bridge until INR >= 2.5 per PCP.

Discharge diagnoses: Bleeding cecal angiodysplasia, treated with APC. Mechanical mitral valve on anticoagulation. Severe aortic stenosis.
Discharge meds: home medications unchanged (warfarin 5 mg, aspirin 81, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5). Enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h until INR >= 2.5.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CBC and INR; GI clinic as needed for recurrence.

medications.sig: Inject 80 mg (0.8 mL) under the skin every 12 hours until INR at least 2.5, per PCP

documents.title: Post-hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 5 days after discharge, with daughter. Admitted 1/7-1/9 for rectal bleeding; tagged RBC scan pointed to the cecum and colonoscopy found angiodysplasia there, treated with APC. No bleeding since. Tired but no worse than before. No dizziness or fainting. Doing the enoxaparin shots.

Discharge summary reviewed. Meds reconciled - unchanged, plus the bridge.

Exam: vitals as charted. A bit pale. Harsh systolic murmur RUSB, mechanical click. Abd soft, NT.

A/P:
1. Cecal angiodysplasia with bleeding, s/p APC - CBC today. Call/ED for recurrence.
2. Mechanical MVR - INR today; stop enoxaparin once >= 2.5. Continue warfarin 5 mg and aspirin.
3. Severe AS - unchanged.
4. DM2/HTN/CKD - BMP, routine visit next month.
Recheck CBC at next visit.

documents.title: INR - Stop Bridge
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in goal. Per PCP stop enoxaparin. Warfarin 5 mg nightly. Pt reports no further bleeding.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine f/u. No bleeding since January. Walking ok with cane outdoors, no falls. Breathing on exertion about the same. Bowels slow as always.

Exam: vitals as charted. Murmur and click as before. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet normal sensation, no lesions.

A/P: DM2 - A1c today. HTN at goal. CKD 3a - BMP. Mechanical MVR - INR today, no change. Angiodysplasia - quiet. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: INR Low
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR a little under goal today. Pt thinks he missed Sunday's dose - weekly pill box was refilled late. No other changes, no bleeding. Per PCP: take 7.5 mg (1 1/2 tablets) tonight only, then back to 5 mg nightly. Recheck in 1 week. Daughter will refill the pill box Saturdays from now on.

events.reason: Progressive fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Fatigue and Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 74 y/o, here because he's been running down for about 3 months - more tired through the day, more winded with ordinary exertion (yard, stairs). No chest pain, no palpitations, no fainting. No visible blood in stool since January that he's noticed. Still on stool softener here and there for his chronic constipation. Meds unchanged - warfarin 5, ASA 81, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.

O: BP 130/80, HR 88. Looks pale. Known harsh AS murmur and mechanical click, otherwise heart exam unchanged. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no liver or spleen enlargement. Rectal: no mass; stool brown, guaiac negative.

Labs (resulted this morning): Hgb 9.2, MCV 72, ferritin 15, iron 30, TIBC 450.

A/P:
1. Iron deficiency anemia, from the cecal angiodysplasia blood loss on warfarin + aspirin. Start ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, take it apart from other meds; it can darken stools and worsen constipation - use the stool softener more regularly if so. Message to GI with today's numbers. CBC in about 3 months.
2. Exertional dyspnea/fatigue - likely anemia on top of his severe AS.
3. Mechanical MVR - INR today, continue warfarin 5 mg.
4. Return sooner for visible bleeding, black stools, dizziness or fainting.

documents.title: Your iron and blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Robert - to recap yesterday: your blood count is low and your iron stores are very low, which explains the tiredness and breathlessness. The iron tablet (ferrous sulfate 325 mg, once a day) is at your pharmacy. It can turn stools dark green or black - that is expected with iron, but if you see red or maroon blood, or feel faint, call us right away. I've sent your results to your GI doctor. We'll recheck the blood count with your August wellness visit.

documents.title: RE: Your iron and blood count
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. Picked them up this afternoon. Do I take it with the warfarin at night or in the morning? - Bob

documents.title: RE: Your iron and blood count
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Morning is best, with a little food if it upsets your stomach, and keep the warfarin at night as usual. Iron doesn't change your INR.

documents.title: Iron - Constipation
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling - since starting iron his bowels are slower and stools very dark. No red or maroon blood, no abdominal pain, no dizziness. Reviewed with PCP: dark stools expected on iron. Use docusate daily rather than as needed, fluids, keep walking. Continue iron. Call if no BM in 3 days, pain, or any red/maroon blood. Pt agrees.

events.reason: Medicare annual wellness visit; anemia recheck

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, daughter along. Feels better than in the spring - more energy, still winded on hills. Taking iron every morning, bowels managed with daily docusate. No red or maroon blood. No falls this year; walking well since the shunt. PHQ-9 2.

Function: independent ADLs; daughter helps with finances and the weekly pill box. Health care proxy: daughter.

Reviewed meds (warfarin 5, ASA 81, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, ferrous sulfate 325 daily, docusate), NKDA, histories.

Exam: vitals as charted. Color better. AS murmur and mechanical click unchanged. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact.

Labs back this afternoon: hemoglobin 12.6 - good response to iron.

Prevention: flu/COVID in October. Pneumococcal, Shingrix, RSV, Tdap (2017) done. Eye exam next month. No further colon cancer screening - GI following.

Plan: continue iron. Lipids, A1c, UACR, CMP, INR pending today. RTC 3 months.

OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 11/11/2025

HPI: 75-year-old man with a mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, severe aortic stenosis, and cecal angiodysplasia treated with APC in 01/2025, with iron deficiency anemia on oral iron since 05/2025. He returns with a week of intermittent, painless bright red blood per rectum. No abdominal pain, no nausea, no change in bowel habit beyond his usual constipation. No dizziness or fainting. His daughter feels he has been more tired lately.

Prior colonoscopies: 01/2024 normal surveillance; 12/2024 no source while not bleeding; 01/2025 cecal angiodysplasia, treated.
Meds: warfarin, aspirin 81, lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, ferrous sulfate.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: no colorectal cancer.

Exam: vital signs stable. Pale. Grade 3/6 systolic murmur, loudest at the right upper sternal border, with a diminished carotid upstroke. Abdomen benign. Rectal: bright red blood, no hemorrhoids, no mass.

Labs: hemoglobin 9.3 g/dL, down from 12.6 in August.

Assessment: Recurrent lower GI bleeding, likely recurrent angiodysplasia, with a drop in hemoglobin on anticoagulation.

Plan: Admit for observation today - CT angiography of the abdomen and repeat colonoscopy, serial hemoglobin. Hospital team to manage anticoagulation with PCP input.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Observation, Lower GI Bleeding
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - OBSERVATION DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Observation 11/11/2025 - 11/13/2025

Reason: recurrent painless hematochezia, hemoglobin 9.3 (12.6 in 08/2025), known cecal angiodysplasia s/p APC 01/2025; mechanical mitral valve on warfarin; severe aortic stenosis.

Allergies: NKDA.

Course:
- Hemodynamically stable throughout. Hemoglobin held steady on serial checks; no transfusion.
- INR in therapeutic range on arrival. After discussion with GI and his PCP, warfarin and aspirin were continued given the mechanical mitral valve and stable counts.
- CT angiography of the abdomen 11/11: no active contrast extravasation; no vascular abnormality; otherwise unremarkable.
- Repeat colonoscopy 11/12: no active bleeding site; prior APC sites in the cecum well healed; no new lesion requiring treatment.
- No further visible bleeding after the first night.

Discharge diagnoses: Lower GI bleeding, presumed recurrent angiodysplasia, no active source found. Acute blood loss anemia superimposed on iron deficiency.
Discharge meds: unchanged (warfarin 5 mg, aspirin 81, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5, ferrous sulfate 325 daily).
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CBC; GI as needed for recurrence.

events.reason: Post-observation follow-up, GI bleeding and anemia

documents.title: Post-hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after 2-night observation stay for recurrent rectal bleeding (Hgb 9.3 from 12.6 in August). CTA and colonoscopy found no active source; old APC sites healed. No further bleeding at home. More tired than in the fall, no dizziness or fainting. Daughter with him.

Observation summary reviewed, meds reconciled - unchanged.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pale. AS murmur and mechanical click. Abd soft, NT.

A/P:
1. Recurrent GI bleeding from angiodysplasia, acute blood loss on top of iron deficiency - CBC today. Continue ferrous sulfate daily.
2. Mechanical MVR - INR today, warfarin 5 mg.
3. Bleeding precautions reviewed again; ED for red or maroon stool, dizziness, fainting.
RTC 3 months, CBC sooner if symptoms.

documents.title: INR today
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Robert, your INR today was fine. No change - 5 mg every evening. Next check mid-January. Happy holidays.
